prompt: How long after a charge does this codebase still allow a refund? A customer just got turned down because their payment was too old.
rationale: Single-file retrieval with a dense distractor cluster. The answer is REFUND_WINDOW_DAYS = 90 in src/billing/refund.ts, and nowhere else in the fixture. The plausible-looking neighbours are src/orders/cancel.ts (imports isRefundable and is the file a caller would reach for), src/billing/charge.ts (payment side, has an idempotency key and a provider call), src/billing/invoice.ts and src/billing/tax.ts (same directory, same money vocabulary), and src/auth/scopes.ts (literally contains the string 'billing:refund' so a naive grep for 'refund' surfaces it). The fixture also holds three other competing time constants that an agent skimming for a number can grab by mistake: TOKEN_TTL_HOURS = 12, HOLD_MINUTES = 15, and maxDelayMs 5000. This is the easy end of the three tasks and exists as the control: if the jev arm cannot beat baseline here it will not beat it anywhere. Verified against the live rank tool over all 34 fixture files: it ranks src/billing/refund.ts first with score 1.000 and present 98%. A live haiku probe exposed a confound that the scorer now closes: 90 days is also Stripe’s documented refund window, so the model volunteered “90 days” from memory with zero tool calls. The scorer therefore requires grounding as well as the number - the transcript must show the repo being inspected, and the answer must either name the source of truth (REFUND_WINDOW_DAYS / billing/refund.ts / isRefundable) or the transcript must show that file being opened. A lucky recall of the Stripe default no longer passes. Live haiku probe on the jev arm with the final prompt: correct and grounded after 4 tool calls and 1 file read, and did NOT call rank.
